title: What If a Mars-Sized Planet Hit Earth?

scenes.text: What if a Mars-sized planet hit Earth? Scientists think it already did, and it made the Moon.
The impactor is called Theia. It was about half Earth's width and roughly a tenth of its mass.
NASA says the blast carried about one hundred million times the energy of the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs.
Chunks of Earth's crust were vaporized and flung into space. Gravity pulled that debris together into the Moon.
The young Moon orbited at roughly one tenth of today's distance, and much of it was molten.
A 2020 study dates it to about 4.4 billion years ago. The Moon you see tonight is what's left of that crash.
